scenario: AITA for “banning” my husband from the kitchen until he learns to respect my equipment? | I love to cook, I’ve been cooking since I was a little kid. I have some good cooking equipment that reflects that fact. My husband decided that he was going to start cooking as well, which I was all for. But he started cooking in the kitchen and damaging my equipment. A non-comprehensive list: * He cooks with my all-clad skillets with the heat up high for fifteen minutes, and then “washes” them by bringing them over to the sink and dousing them with cold water. He says he “likes the sizzle.” At least one of the skillets is warping a bit, it won’t sit straight on the stove anymore and doesn’t cook evenly. * He uses my chef’s knife to scrape crud off the counter. I told him to use my razor blade scraper to do it, he said “well, that would be overkill.” * I have a small toaster oven that acts as a mini-oven, I absolutely love. He butters toast BEFORE putting it in the oven. The fat drips onto the element. He did this so much that I’ve already had to have the element replaced once. He continues to do it and says “we can just replace it again.” * He cooked a tomato sauce in my seasoned cast iron skillet and then ran it through the dishwasher. * He leaves lemon juice, tomato, vinegar spills all over the granite countertops. When I tell him to clean up immediately, he laughs and says, “it’s granite, it’s indestructible!” This all annoyed me so much. I’m annoyed just typing it. Finally I told him that unless he starts actually respecting my equipment, I’m going to put it all under lock and key. He said, “what, you’re banishing me from the kitchen? From my own house?” I said “yes, you’re ruining all of my things.” He implied that it all belonged to him since he “bought it,” but I am fully aware that I had all of this stuff and bought all of this stuff before we got married. AITA? All I want is for him to respect my things. He knows that I hate when he does this stuff but he shouts and yells and calls me over critical every time I try to explain it to him. I’m at my wit’s end.

prediction.raw: **1 (NTA - Not the Asshole)** **Why:** - **Your property, your rules:** You owned all the equipment *before* the marriage, making it your personal property. Even if shared now, you have the right to set boundaries for how it’s used, especially since you’re the primary caretaker and user. - **Damage is real and preventable:** - Thermal shock (cold water on hot All-clad) *does* warp pans permanently. - Using a chef’s knife to scrape counters dulls the blade and can scratch surfaces. - Buttering toast *before* putting it in a toaster oven * will* drip fat onto heating elements, causing damage (as evidenced by the replaced element). - Dishwashing cast iron *ruins* its seasoning and can rust it. - Leaving acidic spills (lemon juice, vinegar, etc.) on granite *does* etch it over time if not cleaned immediately. - **Your husband is dismissive and aggressive:** He’s been repeatedly told these actions are harmful, yet he continues, trivializes your concerns (“ overkill,” “ we can just replace it”), and yields when you try to communicate. This isn’t about “being over critical”— it’s about basic respect for shared (or your) property. - **Your response is proportionate:** "Banning" him from *using specific equipment* is not the same as "banishing him from the kitchen." He can still use the space for other tasks (e.g., microwaving, using non-sensitive appliances, or even cooking with *his own* tools). Locking away damaged items is a logical step to prevent further destruction, not an unreasonable punishment. - **The real issue:** His behavior is the problem. He’s treating your belongings as disposable, ignoring clear instructions, and weaponizing " his own house" rhetoric when he has no claim to *your* pre-marriage assets. **What to do next:** - **Set clear, written boundaries:** List *exactly* which items are off-limits and why (e.g., "All-clad skillets must never be exposed to cold water while hot"). - **Offer alternatives:** "Use this cheaper pan for high-heat cooking" or "Here’s a dedicated scraper for counters." - **Consider a " kitchen rules" agreement:** If he genuinely wants to cook, he can earn access by learning proper care (e.g., taking a class or watching tutorials together). - **If he escalates:** His behavior (yelling, gaslighting) is emotionally manipulative. If he refuses to respect your boundaries, this is a deeper relationship issue that may need couples counseling. **Bottom line:** You’re not the asshole—you’re the one trying to protect your investments and maintain a functional kitchen. His actions are the problem. 💡
